title: Capacity inequality
observableEvidence: Writes an inequality for a real-world constraint, tests candidate values, and describes the solution set on a number line.
prompt: A youth center has room for at most 24 people. There are already 9 people inside. Write an inequality for the number p of additional people, test p = 14 and p = 16, and describe the number-line solution set.
solutionRepresentation: The inequality is 9 + p <= 24, or p <= 15. The value 14 works and 16 does not. The graph has a closed endpoint at 15 and shading to the left.
solutionMethod: Translate 'at most' into less than or equal to, test each candidate in the context, and describe all allowable values from zero through 15.

deterministicValidator.canonicalAnswer: 9 + p <= 24; 14 works, 16 does not; p <= 15 with a closed 15 and shading left
acceptedAnswers: 9 + p <= 24; 14 works, 16 does not; p <= 15 with a closed 15 and shading left
p <= 15; 14 yes, 16 no; closed dot at 15 and ray left
9 + p is at most 24; p can be 0 through 15
deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Accept equivalent inequality notation and a verbal or text description of the closed-left ray and context restriction.

hintSteps.prompt: Translate the phrase 'at most' before choosing the inequality symbol.
hintSteps.question: Can the total equal 24, or must it be less than 24?

hintSteps.prompt: A solution set includes every value that keeps the total within capacity, not just the boundary.
hintSteps.question: Which side of the boundary represents fewer additional people?

accessibilityNotes: Describe the inequality, candidate substitutions, endpoint inclusion, and shading direction in text; no visual number line is required.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: A room holds at most twenty-four people and nine are inside. Model additional people with p, test fourteen and sixteen, and describe all allowed p values.
